packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

text:
packet-19 - blind image reading (unverified)

EXPOSURE / PROCEDURE NOTES
- No proposed identification of the work or author reached me before or during this reading.
- Face B (image-014 overview, tiles 017) carries a modern pencil shelfmark "Stams, STA, Frag. 177v" at the top edge. That is a holding mark, not an identification of the text; I record it because it is visible. A small modern pencil "(9)" at top left of face B is partly under the grey mask (image-015/016).
- I opened only PROMPT.md and the 26 images; I listed the packet directory. Nothing else done.

LAYOUT SURVEY (observations)
- Single sheet, paper-like support, written in long lines, one column, in a fast documentary cursive (one hand on both faces, as far as I can see). Brown ink; no rubrics, no coloured initials, no running titles. Vertical fold/crease with transparent tape repair near the centre on both faces; a hole in the centre of both faces; ragged lower edge with losses on both faces. Faint show-through of the other face visible in the blank left margin.
- Face A (overview image-001; tiles 002-013 in a 4-across grid, rows 002-005, 006-009, 010-013): 13 lines of a calendar notice (dates of movable feasts, transferred feasts) ending "plana & clara," then a new text opening with an enlarged cursive "G" ("Georgius dei gra(tia) Ep(iscop)us Brixinen(sis) ..."), 6+ lines, cut by damage at the bottom. Top of the face is masked grey in images 001-005.
- Face B (overview image-014; tiles 015-026, rows 015-018, 019-022, 023-026): one continuous text of c. 19 lines opening "Georgius dei gr(ati)a ep(iscop)us Brixinen(sis) Vniuersis & singulis ..." with a looped enlarged "G"; paragraph-like sections introduced by "Jtem". Last line damaged.
- Tentative interpretation: both faces look like episcopal mandates/notices addressed to parish clergy (not literary text with commentary). No glosses.

CONVENTION: line numbers below are given per FACE (line 1 = first written line of that face) and each segment is labelled with the tile it is read from and the approximate line position in that tile (tile line counted from top of that tile's visible text). Tiles overlap horizontally; I have joined the overlaps rather than repeating words. Expansions in (), doubt with ?, [illegible] for unread.
